summary: A 1935 7x7 observation cabin on a 60-ft steel tower in Lemhi County, Idaho; newspaper items show fire-season staffing into 1964, and it is drive-up today.

facts.design: 7x7 observation cabin on a 60-ft open steel tower

staffing.status: last documented staffing: September 1964 (newspaper); register says last staffed in the 1950s

access.note: Drive-up on Forest Service roads, per Idaho Fire Lookouts and a climbing guide. No closure notice was found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: A ridge road leads to the summit, per the climbing guide (updated November 2023), which advises checking Forest Service road conditions first and warns of caution if climbing the tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Idaho Fire Lookouts say last staffed in the 1950s. Newspaper items quoted by the Forest Lookouts site show summer staffing in 1962 and 1963, and a family leaving in September 1964. The story reports the 1964 item as the latest documented staffing and notes the conflict.

The register and the Forest Lookouts site give 60 feet. Bing Young's 1982 text, quoted on the climbing guide page, says 70 feet. The brief's height_m of 18.3 (60 ft) is kept, and the story reports both figures.

The register gives 8,359 ft (2,548 m). Firelookout.com gives 8345 ft, Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 8359 ft, and the climbing guide gives 8,333 ft in its header and 8,345 ft in Bing Young's text. The brief's elevation_m of 2547.8 follows the register.

The register uses Salmon-Challis National Forest. Firelookout.com uses Salmon National Forest, and Idaho Fire Lookouts says Boise National Forest. The register's name is used because it is current and matches the brief.

notes_for_editor: Four pages and one climbing guide were read. The register's Built 1935 and the 60-ft figure agree across three sources, and the 70-ft figure is a single quotation of a 1982 book, so treat it as disputed. The staffing record is built from newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts site, not from the newspapers themselves; the 1932 item predates the 1935 steel tower and is the earliest staffing shown here. Abandonment has no date in any source, so no event is recorded for it. Access is set to public from drive-up wording and the absence of any closure notice, not from a Forest Service statement. height_m 18.3 converts the register's 60 ft. The brief's record had no errors to correct. Idaho Fire Lookouts' Boise National Forest label appears to be an error. The Salmon-Challis Facebook post surfaced in search but its text was not read, so the naming of Jules Renaud is not used.
